questions.question: What is the Bill of Rights?
choices: The first ten amendments to the U.S. Constitution
The first ten articles of the Constitution
The preamble to the Declaration of Independence
The final ten amendments to the Constitution

questions.question: When was the Bill of Rights ratified?
Which amendment protects freedom of speech and the press?
Which amendment addresses unreasonable searches and seizures?
Which amendment protects against compelled self-incrimination?
Which amendment protects the right to counsel in criminal prosecutions?
Which amendment prohibits cruel and unusual punishments?
Why did supporters seek a bill of rights?
choices: To grant the president unlimited authority
To provide explicit protections against abuses of government power

questions.question: What does the First Amendment's Establishment Clause address?
What does the right to petition allow people to do?
choices: Require courts to approve every personal request

questions.question: Why does the Fifth Amendment's due process protection matter?
choices: All government action requires unanimous public consent
Government must follow lawful procedures before depriving a person of life, liberty, or property
Every legal dispute must be settled by Congress
Defendants may choose to disregard court orders

questions.question: What does the Ninth Amendment recognize?
choices: Only explicitly listed rights may exist
All powers belong exclusively to the president
States may cancel any federal election
People retain rights beyond those specifically listed

questions.question: What does the Tenth Amendment address?
choices: Powers reserved to the states or the people

questions.question: How did the Bill of Rights originally apply?
choices: It directly governed every foreign nation
It replaced all state criminal law
It primarily restricted the federal government

questions.question: How have many Bill of Rights protections come to apply to states?
choices: Through automatic repeal of all state constitutions
Through Supreme Court interpretations of the Fourteenth Amendment
Through the Twelfth Amendment's election procedures

questions.question: Police seek a warrant to search a home. Which protection is most directly relevant?
A criminal defendant is forced to testify against herself. Which protection is implicated?
choices: The right to keep troops in private homes
The prohibition on titles of nobility
The power to regulate interstate trade

questions.question: A person criticizes government policy peacefully. Which right is most directly involved?
choices: Right to a civil jury trial

questions.question: Why is saying that free speech has no legal limits inaccurate?
choices: The First Amendment protects only elected officials
Some categories of speech and conduct can be lawfully regulated
Any criticism of government is illegal
States may ban every political opinion

questions.question: Which comparison distinguishes the First and Sixth Amendments?
choices: The First creates Congress; the Sixth creates the Cabinet
Both reserve all federal powers to states
The First protects expression; the Sixth protects rights in criminal prosecutions
